evidence: app/package.json:13-16 — react-router ^8.5.0, the current stable release (v8.5.1 published Oct 2026 per npm)
app/react-router.config.ts:3-5 — only ssr:true, the long-default config; no future flags
app/app/lib/api.server.ts:38 — data() utility for 404s, stable since 7.0
app/app/routes/move.tsx:16,34 — Route.MetaFunction/loaderData pattern matches the current v8 API (v8 removed the deprecated meta data arg)
reach.rationale: Zero experimental, preview, or recently-stable framework APIs anywhere; every call is on APIs stable since v7 (Nov 2024) and used in their current v8 form. The only sub-year-old item is Vite's stable resolve.tsconfigPaths config option.

evidence: app/app/lib/api.server.ts:1-60 — all framework-adjacent behavior (data fetching, 404s via data()) is centralized in one server module
app/app/routes.ts:1-10 — routing surface is a flat, minimal config with no lazy/unstable route options
containment.rationale: Nothing experimental to contain; even the patterns closest to framework edges (loader data, error handling) are funneled through a single server-only module.

evidence: app/app/routes/home.tsx:1-2 — filtering via plain useSearchParams/useNavigate rather than any newer revalidation/optimistic-UI APIs
app/app/components/move-tables.tsx:2 — client sorting via plain useState, no experimental hooks
justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used at all, and where the framework offers newer unstable options (v8.5's custom fetch, API-only mode) the app solves them with plain stable primitives — the right conservative choice for a long-lived codebase.

findings.issue: Leftover scaffold comment ('Config options...') and explicit ssr:true (the default) add noise without information
findings.suggestion: Trim the file to the default export or drop the redundant ssr flag and template comment

summary: The app is thoroughly conservative: it pins the current stable React Router 8.5 line and uses only APIs stable since v7, in their current v8 forms. It touches none of the framework's three unstable v8.5 features, so upgrade and breaking-change risk is essentially zero. The only new-ish thing is Vite 8's stable built-in tsconfig-paths resolution, which replaces a community plugin — a good, low-risk adoption.
